name: ReAP (Reflection-Augmented Planning); paper titled "Reflection-Based Memory For Web navigation Agents"
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.02158, cs.AI); no peer-reviewed venue identified as of research date
authors_affiliation: Ruhana Azam (UIUC); Aditya Vempaty (Emergence AI); Ashish Jagmohan (Emergence AI). Lead author Ruhana Azam.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository found; not mentioned in the paper or located via search)
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent LLM web navigation in the WebArena simulated environment (shopping, shopping_admin, map, Reddit, GitLab). The agent (AgentOccam built on gpt-4o-2024-08-06) is augmented with a persistent reflection memory built offline from prior trajectory rollouts. No additional training is required; reflections are induced from prior trajectories (successful and failed) and injected at inference. Two settings tested: (H1) re-doing previously attempted tasks where memory holds reflections of the same tasks; (H2) transfer to similar-but-distinct tasks via an 80-20 train-test split of AgentOccam WebArena trajectories. Reward labels (success/failure) for prior trajectories are available as supervision when constructing reflections.
what_is_retrieved: experiences / reflections: key-value pairs mapping a past user task (key) to a learned reflection/insight gained during navigation (value); three knowledge-type variants tested - One-shot (raw trajectory + reward), Summary (LLM high-level plan summary + reward + failure reason), and Web-Reflection (structured reflection + reward).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes from its own prior experiences (offline-induced knowledge base of reflections from past trajectory rollouts); not a static external doc/KB/API corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: the system retrieves the k=5 most relevant reflections via cosine similarity; no completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes; Reuse: yes (reflections injected into prompt for adaptation to new task); Revise: no (no execution-feedback-driven case revision of stored entries); Retain: partial/offline (reflections are stored once during offline BuildMemory from prior trajectories, not continuously retained online during deployment). Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=no, Retain=partial-offline].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not explicitly frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it frames itself as reflection-based memory / retrieval-augmented planning, realizing retrieve-and-reuse mechanisms under a different name.
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule / distilled insight: a task-keyed reflection (free-text key insight about the website/task, e.g., 'Allrecipes.com does not have a filter for preparation time'). Variants also include full-trajectory (One-shot raw (s,a,...,r) sequence) and high-level summary units, but the headline ReAP unit is the distilled reflection.
index_source: Growing memory, offline-induced: the retrievable store is built offline (BuildMemory) from prior trajectory rollouts of the base agent (AgentOccam); in H1 from a single rollout per task, in H2 from 80% training-split trajectories. Frozen at inference (not grown online at test time).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index keyed by task-instruction embeddings (each entry stores task text, reflection R(tau), and Embed(task)); retrieval is over flat cosine-similarity nearest neighbors.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf text-embedding model with cosine similarity). Selected embedding model: gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct (also evaluated llama8b-nnetnav-wa, text-embedding-3-large/small, all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a pretrained embedding model with cosine similarity; no contrastive, LM-feedback, task-effectiveness, or RL training of the retriever. Embedding model choice (gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct) was selected by qualitative inspection of task-cluster separation, not trained.
query_construction: Raw task-instruction query, lightly templated as "Go to {start_url}, {intent}" (e.g., 'Go to MAP, Which US states border Illinois?'), then embedded.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single query is formed from the new task instruction and used to retrieve reflections before/at planning time; not per-step or trajectory-level.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per task at the start (top-5 reflections injected into the prompt before the agent acts).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered once at task start by the ReAPPrompt routine; no confidence/uncertainty/learned-router/reflection-token trigger.
reranking: None. A single dense cosine-similarity ranking selects the top-5; no separate reranking stage (cross-encoder, RRF, etc.).
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time (top-5 reflections concatenated directly into the prompt). Note: the reflections themselves are pre-distilled/compressed at memory-construction time (Summary and Web-Reflection variants), but no post-retrieval rerank/decompose/distill/filter step is applied.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions; the indexed items are task-keyed reflections, not tool docs).
index_content_separation: No explicit progressive-disclosure / index-then-content separation; the embedding key (task) and the stored content (reflection) are co-stored in the same entry and the reflection is loaded directly when retrieved.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol; WebArena environment, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool store).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tool retrieval; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-5 retrieved reflections (K1...Kk) are concatenated with the current task instruction and fed to the base agent (Agent(t_i (+) K1 (+) ... (+) Kk)), guiding planning/acting without any fine-tuning. Functions as case-adaptation via in-context insights.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars/insights at plan time: reflections are injected once into the agent prompt before the agent plans and acts; the base AgentOccam agent then runs its standard multi-step planning/acting loop conditioned on these insights (retrieve-then-plan).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-task: retrieval happens once per task before the navigation rollout; reflections are not re-retrieved per CoT-step or per action within the rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation: retrieved reflections/insights are provided in-context and the LLM agent adapts its plan to the new task; for the One-shot variant a verbatim trajectory+reward exemplar is used. No execution-feedback-driven revision of stored cases or RL reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/insight as free text (Web-Reflection and Summary variants: high-level insights, plan summaries, failure reasons, shortcuts, feedback). The One-shot variant instead injects a raw trajectory with reward label.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Primarily a distilled strategy/insight (state-aware reflection/guideline about the site and task), contrasted in ablations with raw-trajectory (One-shot) and plan-summary representations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited/none explicit. The reflections are pre-distilled to key insights (rather than full noisy trajectories) which the authors argue transfers better, but there is no dedicated relevance-evaluator, retriever-aware training, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware SFT. The paper notes some negative transfer on previously successful tasks.
memory_type: episodic (reflection-based key-value memory of past task->insight pairs); functions as a persistent reflection memory across sessions/tasks.
write_back: True (offline). The system writes reflections derived from prior trajectories into the knowledge base during the BuildMemory phase; however, it does not write back new experiences online during test-time deployment in the reported experiments.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is built offline from prior rollouts / the 80% training split and is frozen at inference; the paper does not grow memory during test-time evaluation.
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure (reflective): reflections are generated and stored from BOTH successful and failed prior trajectories, with reward labels and reasons-for-failure captured. The write happens offline during memory construction (after self-reflection over a completed trajectory), not per-step and not human-validated; it is not triggered online during deployment.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure (both stored): a central contribution is leveraging both successful and failed past experiences. Reflections from failed trajectories drive the largest gains (+20 points H1, +28 points H2 on previously-failed tasks). Reward labels mark success/failure; not purely contrastive but both polarities are stored and retrieved.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only: entries are added during BuildMemory and not subsequently mutated, deduped, refined, or pruned.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed cosine-similarity top-k over off-the-shelf embeddings; not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory. No sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks; one base agent (AgentOccam) uses its own reflection store.
benchmarks: WebArena (70-task subset for H1 with single rollout per task; for H2, publicly available AgentOccam WebArena trajectories split 80-20 train/test). Sites: shopping, shopping_admin, map, Reddit, GitLab.
baselines: AgentOccam (base agent, gpt-4o-2024-08-06, no memory) - reported as the 'N/A'/baseline. Knowledge-type variants compared internally: One-shot & Reward Label, Summary & Reward Label, Web-Reflection & Reward Label. Prior memory approaches discussed (ICAL, AgentWorkflow, WILBUR) are positioned against but not run as quantitative baselines.
key_metrics: Success Rate (SR, primary); plus cost-efficiency metrics: total tokens, prompt tokens, task-completion time (Tct, seconds), and average number of steps.
headline_result: ReAP improves baseline (AgentOccam) by +11 points overall SR and +28-29 points on previously failed tasks (H2 transfer setting, top-5 reflections, gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct, 70 WebArena tasks / 80-20 split), while reducing average steps by 34.7% (and ~29.1% in H2). In H1 (re-doing prior tasks): +5 points overall, +20 points on previously failed tasks.
ablations: Knowledge-type ablation across One-shot vs Summary vs Web-Reflection: Summary and Reflection give +11 points (H2) vs One-shot +6 points, and Reflection gives best SR while reducing step count; Summary gives best token efficiency (~74% token reduction in H1). Positive-only vs Negative-only vs combined example sources: failed-trajectory reflections drive the largest gains on previously-failed tasks. Embedding-model selection (gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct vs llama8b-nnetnav-wa, text-embedding-3-large/small, all-MiniLM-L6-v2) via task-cluster separation; gte-Qwen2-7B-instruct chosen (+12 points on both task categories). Temperature/determinism effect (Appendix B.1).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR) and cost are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are not reported. Embedding quality is assessed only qualitatively via t-SNE and cosine-similarity matrices (Appendix C), not as decoupled retrieval scores.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome (SR), augmented with process/efficiency proxies: number of steps, re-prompt reductions, tokens, and completion time, which reflect trajectory quality. No reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported in detail. ReAP reduces steps by ~15.4% (H1) and 29.1% (H2) overall, up to 37.1% on previously failed tasks; Summary cuts H1 token usage ~74% (221k->58k total) and time 51% (682s->334s); H2 Reflection uses 83k vs 221k baseline tokens. Tradeoff: Summary best for tokens, Reflection best for SR with reduced steps; One-shot can increase tokens (up to 1095k in negative-only H2).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: top k=5 reflections retrieved by cosine similarity and concatenated into the prompt. No adaptive/precision-driven k or explicit token budget cap; injected reflection size varies by knowledge type (distilled reflections/summaries are far smaller than raw One-shot trajectories).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; reuses WebArena, a 70-task subset for H1 and an 80-20 split of public AgentOccam trajectories for H2).
builds_on: AgentOccam (Yang et al. 2024a, base web agent + AgentOccam-Judge); WebArena (Zhou et al. 2023, environment); self-reflection methods (Reflexion - Shinn et al. 2023; Self-Refine - Madaan et al. 2023); insight/strategy-memory methods (Suzgun et al. 2025, the most conceptually similar; Thought-Retriever - Feng et al. 2024; Buffer-of-Thoughts - Yang et al. 2024b); RAG (Lewis et al. 2020). Authors' prior work: Azam et al. 2024 (multimodal auto-validation / self-refinement in web agents).
contrasts_with: Prior trajectory-storing memory systems that store complete workflows/trajectories rather than distilled insights: ICAL (Sarch et al. 2025, iteratively improving in-context examples), AgentWorkflow (Wang et al. 2024b, parses/stores trajectory sub-goals), and WILBUR (Lutz et al. 2024, stores trajectory summaries). ReAP contrasts by focusing on key reflections/insights (not full workflows) and by explicitly using both successful and failed experiences.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience-based planning): an experience/reflection-memory web-navigation method in the lineage of self-reflection (Reflexion) + memory-augmented agents, positioned among insight-distillation memory approaches (Suzgun et al. 2025, Buffer-of-Thoughts) and trajectory-memory web agents (ICAL, AgentWorkflow, WILBUR).
